chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Nadr from 'Asim from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a mukatab (a slave who has contracted manumission) whose walayah (manumission lineage) was stipulated to be with him upon his freedom. He married a walidah (female slave) of another man, and she bore him a child. His child was freed, and then the mukatab died, and his child inherited him. They disputed regarding his child, asking: 'Who inherits him?' He said, 'He attached his child to the mawali (freedmen) of his father.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in this report is that the mukatab, once he fulfilled his manumission contract, became free. When he subsequently married a walidah of another person and was blessed with children from her, the children became attached to him due to his freedom, and their walayah became for the one who possessed the walayah of their father. If the children had been slaves belonging to the master of the woman or to her manumitter, their walayah would have been for them, and they would not have attached to their father.

And that which indicates this is what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated in his book, so he mentioned thus: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I asked him about a free woman whom I married to my slave, and she bore him children. Then the slave went to someone else, and I freed him. To whom does the walayah of their children belong? To me, if their mother is my freedwoman, or to the one who freed their father?
He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'If the mother is free, the father draws the walayah. And if you are the one who freed him, there is no drawing of walayah for their father.'

key_terms.جَرَّ الْوَلاَء: To draw or attract the walayah lineage
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a certain sum for his freedom
key_terms.وَلاَء: Manumission lineage or the right of inheritance between a master and his freed slave

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the walayah of children born to a freed slave who marries a female slave?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'jarr al-wala'' (linking manumission lineage to the father) in cases of mixed-status marriages, distinguishing between a mukatab who becomes fully free versus a slave manumitted by a third party. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary highlights that the children's allegiance follows the father's status at the time of marriage and manumission, a key juristic distinction in Shia fiqh regarding inheritance and social ties. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the father's manumitter as the primary link for walayah when the mother remains enslaved, contrasting with other schools that might prioritize the mother's master.
